meaning: Two of the eight demands u18c itemised were answerable by reading the installed tree harder rather than by any new decision, and both readings were taken. The production build was run again on the result. It is still red, and this record is the red one: the diagnostic total fell from 110 to 57, every family that moved is named with its before and after count, and every demand that remains is itemised — including two the falling census made visible for the first time. No demand was answered by an edit this record does not name, no artifact was emitted, and no parity or determinism claim is made or possible.

tree.reuse: The stage tree u18b staged was reused and the composed changeset was rewritten over it from the pristine source, exactly as u18c did. Two things follow that this record states rather than glosses. Every file the changeset changes is rewritten from the pristine tree on each application, so those bytes are the composition's. Files that only a capability round has ever touched are not rewritten by the changeset and were therefore inherited from u18c — which is why the fork and barrel capabilities report almost nothing changed here: they had already run on those files and found their own work in place. The measure that is not affected by this is the diff against the pristine tree, and it is the one reported below.

acquisition.purpose: None. No package was installed, no manifest was changed and no network was reached in this unit; the closure u18c resolved was read, not altered.

adapterChanges: `ClosureFileReading` — the reading the webpack tilde capability asks the file system for — now carries a second, optional question: does the installed package's own `exports` map answer this subpath. The capability consults the map before the sass file candidates, because a package that publishes an `exports` map is reachable through it and not through arbitrary paths beneath it, and falls back to the file candidates for a package that publishes no map, which is how every package of the era was reached. A reading that supplies no map answer is asked only the file question, so every caller written before the map existed behaves exactly as it did.

A `suggested-export-rename` source capability. A library that renames an export and a library that deletes one leave the same shape at the import site — a name the installed package does not have — and the difference cannot be read off the spelling. TypeScript already computes it: TS2724 carries the compiler's own resolution of the successor against the installed declaration files, and TS2305 is the same absence with no successor offered. The capability consumes only the first. The suggestion is then checked rather than trusted: the successor must be on the package's measured root export surface and the name being replaced must be absent from it, or the rename is refused by name. The rewrite is a binding rename — an aliased import has only its exported name replaced, an unaliased one has its exported name and every resolved reference to its binding replaced, and only when the successor name is free in the module's root scope, because a rename that collided with an existing declaration would silently change which symbol the references mean. A subpath import, an incomplete surface reading, and a position that is not an import specifier are three further refusals.

notEstablished: The build is red. No artifact was emitted, nothing was executed, and no parity, determinism or logical-name statement against the era lane is possible or attempted. The build was run once, because a second run of a build that fails in the TypeScript program before the Sass compiler would establish nothing about the Sass random() nondeterminism the era lane recorded.

A diagnostic census is not a measure of remaining work. 110 → 57 says what the compiler reported twice. Most of the fall is the template census downstream of one module that now resolves, and two of the demands on the list above are larger in this census than in the last one for exactly the same reason: more of the application is visible to the compiler than was before.
The five sass at-rules resolve against the installed package's exports map. Nothing here establishes that they compile, because the sass compiler was not reached.

The two renames the compiler resolved are renames of names, checked against the installed surfaces. Nothing establishes that NgChartsModule behaves as ChartsModule did or that a ChartDataset is populated the way a ChartDataSets was; no browser opened anything and the chart configuration those names sit next to is itself an itemised demand.
The era lane's recorded Sass random() nondeterminism is untouched. No source was seeded, neutralised or modified.
